requirements.verify: integration/security: save and read personal/group knowledge through actual persistence; reject wrong-tenant, wrong-Space and forged bindings.
integration/security: exercise allowed same-scope relations, approved sharing and forged cross-scope object/manifest/checkpoint relations; denied mutations leave no durable rows or bytes published.

integration/security: use real local authenticated service and non-owner PostgreSQL transactions; deny forged actor/payer/scope, expired/revoked sessions and authority changes around asynchronous/commit boundaries.
integration/security: eligible group sources succeed; personal-to-group and partly authorized audience requests are refused before private content enters generation and at output.
security: mark restricted fixture payloads/titles, inspect actual generator inputs, responses, manifests/logs and durable state after refusals; all unauthorized disclosure/mutation counts are zero.
integration/security: private-note/group-volume writes and restricted-history guest access are refused; allowed group-readable files remain governed by their actual storage grant.
integration/security: inspect real fixture role/grant properties and attempt worker/unauthorized direct access; rerun unchanged foundation and identity guards through controller.

integration/security/recovery: inject current-authority outage with populated caches and restored old grants; observe no affected content/generator input or durable unauthorized write, and recover allowed service after authority returns.

review/security: map every new record to its owner and existing integration; adversarial stored/model data cannot create approvals, budgets, protected receipts, control changes or canonical memory through a generated context file.

integration/security: read actual retained object/volume/checkpoint/backup files, verify fixture private plaintext is absent, and decrypt/recover the exact acknowledged payload using authorized fixture material across recreation.

integration/security/recovery: alter persisted ciphertext/metadata binding and use wrong/missing fixture keys; affected reads/restore fail with no payload or false recovery success; correct material recovers unchanged bytes.

review/security: inspect the documented inventory against real retained files/database fields/derived stores and logs using marked private data; every copy is covered by the stated encryption/retention boundary.
review/security: inspect fixture setup, persisted outputs and key documentation; confirm only repository-reproducible synthetic material is used and production managed-key claims remain unqualified.
security/review: inspect logs, audit rows and diagnostic export after save/ask/delete/failure; verify redacted payload handling, declared retention and scoped access.

integration/review: inspect actual PostgreSQL records/outbox and stored object/volume manifests; rebuild a derived view without granting it canonical authority; show a volume snapshot cannot substitute for a metadata transaction.
integration: save, recreate service, correct and recall real records; inspect canonical revision/history and permitted manifests for exact recorded provenance rather than inferred/generated fields.

unit/integration: exercise supported status transitions and recall eligibility; pending/disputed/expired/deleted records cannot be presented as current verified decisions, and provenance preserves uncertainty.
integration: store ordinary discussion and a proposed inference, then ask for the accepted decision; neither becomes approved by implication, while an explicit authorized save succeeds.

integration/recovery: interrupt transaction before/after revision/event/outbox writes; verify all required canonical pieces commit together or roll back, and invalid secret/retention admission leaves no accepted record.

integration/recovery: observe commit and response order, fail/intercept actual writes and recreate service; every Saved here response resolves to the same durable accepted revision, and pending/failure states remain distinct.

integration/recovery: interrupt byte upload, manifest persistence and metadata publication in turn; fresh reads never expose a dangling published artifact and fully confirmed publication returns exact bytes/digest.
integration/recovery: create interrupted uploads, observe no serving/publication, then exercise declared quarantine/cleanup while proving unrelated fixture objects are untouched.

unit/integration/security: reject missing/forged bindings, expired ordinary writes and stale revision commands; serialize/parse the supported command contract without silently discarding required security fields.

integration/concurrency/recovery: race identical and incompatible retries, including service recreation; count one canonical revision/event/outbox/receipt set for identical retries and explicit conflict for changed binding.

integration/recovery: lose actual commit acknowledgement, recreate caller, query original key during commit/rollback/lock-timeout windows, observe exact receipt or truthful unknown/absence and no duplicate canonical commit.

integration/concurrency/recovery: two real writers read one revision, contend on incompatible changes and include a recreated stale writer; current accepted head is preserved and the losing writer receives inspectable conflict/review.
integration/concurrency: concurrently persist independent facts through actual storage and read both via a fresh service; no unnecessary global overwrite or missing record.

integration: correct one real saved claim beside unrelated knowledge; verify supersession chain/history/current recall and unchanged unrelated record, with disputed claims not hidden or treated as certain.

unit/integration/security: exercise similar values from separate sources/scopes and permitted identical retries; inspect responses and canonical records for correct nonmerging and no cross-tenant existence disclosure.

security/integration: save/correct adversarial memory and edit a generated context proposal; inspect owners/call counters to prove no behavior release, grant, check receipt or controller completion is created.
integration/security: populate eligible and forbidden stored sources, capture actual generator/reranker/enrichment inputs, and verify only currently eligible content crosses each supported boundary.

integration/concurrency/security: pause a real answer after eligible retrieval, then delete/revoke or change audience before disclosure; no subsequent disallowed answer/manifest publication, while unchanged eligible publication succeeds.

integration: inspect manifests from actual saved-decision answers, delayed-index and restored journeys; all fields identify the real selected records/current authority and hidden titles/content are absent.
integration/recovery: commit a decision with indexing paused, delayed and failed; retrieve real canonical bytes before index repair, observe watermark/limitation and no permission bypass.
integration: ask with absent/expired/disputed evidence and a historical record; assert explicit safe limitation/next action and no fabricated saved decision or live-inspection result.

security/integration: use same billing team across rooms, stale populated caches, permission/source revisions and revocation; inspect allowed outputs and generator inputs for zero cross-scope leakage.

integration/concurrency/recovery: fail enrichment after canonical commit, recreate processor and process an older queued summary after correction; original acknowledged record survives and accepted head is not silently overwritten.

integration/security/review: demonstrate stored-source Ask composition with installed identity/model/budget owners; deny stale/ineligible profiles or missing budgets before local call, inspect original binding/manifest, and label paid or unsupported calls as disabled.

e2e/integration: explicitly save a decision, recreate service, Ask what was decided, assert selected stored bytes affect the answer and permitted source/version manifest, and observe zero Space-computer starts; deterministic answer path is labelled local.

integration/security: exercise real saved-decision service routing and source broker calls; inspect supplied capabilities/dispatches and test attempted file/shell/effect proposals are denied with zero target writes.
integration/concurrency/recovery: instrument the actual service/computer boundary and run each listed journey; assert each computer-route counter is zero while authorized answers remain useful.

integration/security: request unsupported live inspection and inject service failures; verify safe refusal/capability next action and no hidden computer, disk, local-host or unapproved-route dispatch.

integration/concurrency: queue an Ask/save in Space A, switch to B, complete and recreate service; A retains original binding, B sees only permitted records and forged currentSpace does not change authority.

unit/integration: exercise each supported setting independently and in combination, inspect selected content and created canonical records, and verify task-only/no-save behavior plus truthful filesystem/retention explanation.
integration/security: save to the resolved personal/group binding; if copy is supported, test allowed/denied export, otherwise refuse it explicitly; no silent private extraction or new source grant.
integration: inventory retention classes, advance an explicit fixture clock/duration, and verify eligible-before/expired-after behavior for real canonical records, files and supported derivatives.
integration/security: permitted fixture data operators can delete/restore; readers/members, forged operators and revoked/expired grants are denied with no durable lifecycle effect.
integration/recovery: delete/expire real persisted records, recreate services, inspect durable tombstones/invalidation work and confirm future recall/publication remains unavailable.

integration/security/concurrency: revoke a source before and during recall/generation/derived processing; future content is suppressed; any supported copied-publication exception requires a separately recorded, current grant.

integration/security/concurrency: remove a fixture member with active retrieval and cached context; test both race orders and subsequent reads/outputs, including recreation, for zero disallowed disclosure.

integration/recovery: persist a multi-level dependency graph, apply each restriction, inspect durable affected descendants and actual retrieval/output refusal; unsupported descendant classes are explicitly inventoried rather than claimed qualified.

integration/concurrency/recovery: queue jobs before delete/revoke/correct, release them afterward and after processor restart, including duplicate delivery; canonical/derived reads stay denied or current and no stale writer restores restricted bytes.

integration/recovery: fail descendant processing after partial progress, observe truthful pending state and immediate serving denial, recreate processor and retry to completion without duplicate mutations or content resurrection.
integration/recovery: correct real source-backed knowledge with an old cached/indexed answer, process/retry derived updates and inspect canonical current recall before/after propagation.
integration/review: exercise permitted, denied, repeated and partially propagated forget requests; inspect user/operator impact/status fields and documented external/backup limitations.

integration/concurrency/recovery: observe real contested operations in both orderings, duplicate delete and crashes around tombstone/invalidation writes; finite suite has zero future prohibited recall/publication/resurrection.
integration/review: persist/checkpoint supported classes separately, interrupt uncommitted editing, recreate service and inspect actual recovery plus Saved/unsaved/uncheckpointed status per class.
integration/concurrency: race two actual promotions from one base, verify exact accepted bytes/manifest and explicit losing conflict; unauthorized promotion leaves canonical files unchanged.

integration/recovery/security: save a draft, recreate service, inspect original version and audience, then reconnect a stale draft against a newer accepted version and verify conflict/retention without overwrite.

integration/recovery: close/recreate actual service/process/storage clients after confirmed saves and interrupted writes, then read exact committed bytes/records and accurately expose unavailable unsaved work.

integration/concurrency/recovery: retain a stale writer across actual recreation/restore, advance the authoritative revision/generation and attempt save/promotion; denied writes leave current canonical state unchanged.

integration/recovery: create real backup/checkpoint files and canonical metadata, restore into a fresh owned destination and recreated service, compare surviving records/manifests/bytes and perform a real restored saved-decision Ask; in-memory serialization alone fails.

integration/recovery/security: restore a complete backup plus corrupt, missing-byte, mismatched-manifest and incomplete variants; assert exact good recovery and inspectable blocked state with no dangling published record in each bad case.

integration/recovery/concurrency: back up real data, delete/expire/revoke afterward, restore older copies and observe the serving/rebuild barrier; eligible survivors succeed but restricted records/files/descendants cannot enter inputs or outputs.

integration/recovery: back up revision N, correct to N+1, restore the old backup and Ask; canonical current authority resolves the accepted revision or blocks serving with a stated freshness limitation, never silently presents N as current.

integration/recovery/security: restore with current ledger/policy missing, unavailable or stale, and crash around barrier transitions; no affected serving occurs until authoritative freshness is proven.

integration/recovery/concurrency: interrupt actual restore before/after metadata/byte/restriction phases, recreate operator/service and repeat the bound operation; inspect persisted recovery state, canonical identities and served content.

integration/recovery/security: include fixture stale operation/approval/generation/credential references, restore and inspect dispatch/model/write counters plus authority state; recovery causes no effect replay or grant/session resurrection.

review/integration/recovery: compare class inventory and operating procedure to executed crash/restore observations, acknowledged revisions and checkpoint timestamps; document what was preserved and what was lost without invented production RPO/RTO.

integration/review: inspect allowed/denied/conflict/expiry/index-outage/encryption/restore-failure outcomes for safe status and actionable resolver; no indefinite success spinner or invented completed action.
review/integration: controller executes node g1-storage/scripts/check.mjs and verifies requested plan/evidence paths exist and describe the implemented candidate.

requirements.verify: integration: controller runs the check from a fresh candidate/dependency state; verify strict compiler success and actual executed assertions for canonical storage, saved answers and restore instead of prebuilt/canned outputs.
integration/review: inspect and exercise harness failure cases for each condition; require successful nonempty execution per mandatory behavior group and zero failed/cancelled/skipped/TODO tests.

integration/e2e/security: controller observes actual stored bytes/records, generator inputs, manifests, competing writers, propagation and recreation/restore; assert prohibited counters zero and positive outcomes, not schema/label-only tests or refuse-all behavior.

regression/review: unchanged retained-source/raw hash guards and existing required controller checks pass; inspect diff for only new increment or authorized additive paths, leaving previous worktree/controller state untouched.
regression/review: inspect controller job definitions/results for unchanged identity, foundation and retained baselines including Electron; local diagnostics are labelled separately from acceptance.

review: audit evidence-to-current-controller-output links and hashes/fingerprints, preserve raw failures, and confirm no unsigned author claim substitutes for registered reviews or controller completion.

review: inspect requested plan/evidence and linked increment documents against actual build dependencies, owner boundaries, supported classes and test obligations; rollback must preserve external effects/tombstones rather than imply undo.

requirements.source: Current goal, Constraints and Needs approval first; docs/loop/agent-fabric-g1-f05-storage/product-brief.md:82,94
requirements.verify: review/security: inspect actions, scripts and evidence for local synthetic-only execution, disabled external routes and official approval records before any restricted action; no elapsed-time or inferred approval.

integration/security/review: inspect fixture identities and cleanup observations, preserve preexisting fixture census, exercise cleanup failure and verify no global prune/kill/unowned path deletion or external fallback.
review: inspect recorded requirements and turn diff/tool history; stage submission is requirements-only and controller owns progression.
review/integration: follow the documented local journey against actual fixture persistence and inspect user-readable outputs; any exception to this intended default is documented.
review: trace each recorded mandatory obligation to an executed assertion or explicit pending external gate in the matrix; no interface-only coverage is counted as behavior.

review/integration: inspect local save/recovery/lifecycle explanations and existing model charge contract integration; document retained fixture classes and clarify that actual cloud billing is not measured.
review: if added, map each optional fixture to an existing obligation and preserve mandatory coverage and local-only limits.
review: list each untested deployment/storage guarantee with missing environment evidence and next gate; local encrypted-file/restore results qualify only their finite local profile.
review/human: document fixture durations/keys as test parameters and unresolved external decisions as pending; before external use obtain the actual authorized policy-owner decision through loop_ask.

review/security: inventory implemented serving paths and local reauthorization tests; explicitly mark real broker/stream/signed-link guarantees pending until approved-provider revocation tests and exposure windows exist.

review: evidence separates executable local source/route behavior from missing real host/kernel/image/service isolation; next qualification gate is named without running remote resources in this stage.
review: acceptance identifies reused local identity qualification and explicitly pending enterprise SSO/human gates rather than equating fixtures with production identity.
review: label actual answer adapter/profile and synthetic accounting; list missing approved real model/gateway/data-region evidence and leave external enablement gated.
review: preserve required existing client regressions while acceptance records missing physical/platform and representative-user evidence; no new GUI is demanded by F05.

review: separate baseline implemented requirements and later-depth/external obligations in plan/evidence; unrelated modules and ledger rows remain pending, with no omission of mandatory F05 behaviors.

review/performance: audit evidence for measured boundaries, actual samples/conditions and explicit pending production measurements; roadmap pilot numbers are identified as targets, not local achieved SLAs.

review/security: retain unresolved findings and profile limitations visibly; confirm controller acceptance and independent review stay separate from author evidence and unaffected ledger obligations are not closed.

integration: change source revision/validity and knowledge head with an older index/context present; inspect exact source-backed answer/manifest and visible conflict/limitation, with authorized current decisions still retrievable.
